reason: Output is emitted via json_encode with an explicit Content-type: application/json header, so DB values are never rendered in an HTML context and no XSS sink exists in this snippet.
This is an auto-generated TypeScript declaration file with static compile-time import type references only; there is no runtime file access or user-controlled path, so CWE-22 is inapplicable.
The logSQL method performs no outbound HTTP/network request at all (it only formats and logs SQL and runs a local DB EXPLAIN with the original bindings), so SSRF (CWE-918) is inapplicable.

This is a PHPUnit test that asserts the HTML writer renders a malicious hyperlink payload as inert cell text; test code with a fixed fixture and no untrusted input reaching a browser is not itself an XSS vulnerability.

User-controlled $descricao (from extract($_REQUEST)) is stored and echoed back via json_encode without a Content-Type: application/json header, so the response defaults to text/html and json_encode does not escape angle brackets, allowing script injection when the endpoint is loaded directly.

listar() echoes DB rows (user-populated fields) and even raw PDOException objects via json_encode with no application/json Content-Type header and no HTML escaping, so the text/html default response can render stored markup, enabling XSS.

This is the CSRF protection middleware itself: unsafe methods always reach verifyToken(realToken, sentToken) and a tampered or missing cookie token fails verification, so the snippet implements rather than lacks CSRF defense.
The method parses an already-opened file handle passed in by the caller and never constructs a filesystem path from user input, so there is no traversal sink in the shown code.
Raw $_POST['cor'] is concatenated directly into an INSERT statement executed via $pdo->query with no parameterization or escaping, a textbook SQL injection.
This is a pure configuration interface with property getters and no output rendering or HTML sink whatsoever, so CWE-79 is inapplicable.
